[JBS Praxis](mailto:praxisjbs@gmail.com) [tom.asaah@jbspraxis.com](mailto:tom.asaah@jbspraxis.com) [elishaokoh897@gmail.com](mailto:elishaokoh897@gmail.com) [tomblakeasaah@gmail.com](mailto:tomblakeasaah@gmail.com) [victorjerome34@gmail.com](mailto:victorjerome34@gmail.com)

Project kickoff with technical architecture and module ownership established via milestones.

## **Project architecture and milestone structure**

* The project is structured across 12 milestones, utilizing milestone 0 to establish core foundations.  
* Elisha configured an 18GB RAM server with a 240GB SSD supporting 4 distinct subdomains.  
* The technical stack utilizes Node.js, BullMQ, Redis, PostgreSQL 16, Chromium, and Nginx proxy routing.

## **Module ownership and logic sourcing**

* Team members assume full end-to-end ownership of assigned modules to streamline development.  
* Core operations adopt over 70% of existing logic while maintaining custom user interfaces.  
* The attendance module spans multiple areas, including employee self-service, settings, registers, and device tracking.

## **Access control and permission management**

* System access operates through a role-based permissions matrix gating modules by assigned roles.  
* Administrative views remain restricted to operations and HR, while employees access limited self-service features.

## **System architecture and services configuration**

* Godwin-Okoh Elisha outlined shared SRC modules, standalone services, real-time sockets, and background job workers.  
* Godwin-Okoh Elisha noted milestone 0 is covered while milestones 1 through 11 will be added later.  
* Storage services support S3, local, Amazon, or Google Drive configurations.

## **AI assistant data access and pagination**

* Tom-Blake Asaah noted that the AI assistant reads the database and provides UI deep links.  
* Tom-Blake Asaah proposed pagination limits of 25 items for AI data fetching to prevent server timeouts.

## **Home module dashboard and alert engine**

* Tom-Blake Asaah renamed the command center module to home to maintain simplicity in naming conventions.  
* Tom-Blake Asaah designed the home dashboard to be role-sensitive, displaying tailored KPIs for specific users.  
* Alert rules monitor metrics like attendance breaches and inactive partnerships exceeding 30 days.  
* Tom-Blake Asaah restricted report generation modules exclusively to managers and the CEO.  
* The staging database utilizes mock data to test dashboard visualizations prior to live deployment.

## **Frontend migration and mobile layout**

* Tom-Blake Asaah proposed translating HTML reference templates into a React and Vite setup.  
* Tom-Blake Asaah flagged that current layouts require a dedicated mobile design with optimized icons.

## **Repository management and data imports**

* Godwin-Okoh Elisha announced that the project repository will be hosted on the JBS GitHub account for collaborators.  
* Tom-Blake Asaah requested organizational staff lists from the client to test import engines and seed staging data.

## **Next steps**

- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Distribute documentation: Forward the documentation document regarding the application architecture to the group.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Update admin script: Modify the create admin script to seed full employee information instead of just email and password. Ensure the script follows the complete payload requirement for system integrity.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Develop documentation: Generate comprehensive engineering guides, including backend, frontend, and feature-specific architecture documents within the repository. Populate the README and ensure the progress markdown file automatically updates with project status.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Grant repo access: Invite team members to collaborate on the private repository to ensure full access to the project code.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Limit Pagination: Set a pagination limit of 25 items per page across the entire system to prevent server crashes.  
- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Create Mobile Design: Develop a responsive mobile design for the application to replace the current heavy sidebar and text-heavy interface.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Setup Project Repository: Push the project to the JBS GitHub repository and invite all team members as collaborators.  
- [ ] \[The group\] Prepare Attendance Presentation: Gain a full understanding of the attendance end to end process to present during the meeting scheduled at 5:00 PM.  
- [ ] \[Godwin-Okoh Elisha\] Send Backend Documentation: Share the updated backend Markdown file with the group.  
- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Submit Meeting Transcript: Provide the transcript of the current meeting.

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C1Iu8__tdZA6PFN4kJNGgVp0dk1DCc3dLDQ5xBZNePU/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.5gdqm2ahkzkn) 

### **Summary**

Project kickoff with technical architecture and module ownership established via milestones.

**Milestone And Architecture Setup**  
Project structure established across 12 milestones with Node backend and server specifications detailed.

**Role Based Access Control**  
Module permissions and access matrices defined for operational workflows.

**Dashboard And Frontend Guidelines**  
React migration planned with strict pagination limits and role sensitive dashboard views.

### **Decisions**

## Aligned

* **System-wide pagination limit configuration standard** The pagination limit is established at 25 records per page across the entire system for both the backend and frontend.

* **AI assistant database access and pagination** The AI assistant will operate in a read-only mode providing deep links for UI navigation and enforce pagination limits in batches of 25 for data fetching.

* **Module renaming from command center to home** The command center module is renamed to home to ensure simplicity in module naming conventions.

* **HTML template translation to React and Vite** The HTML reference files will be translated into React and Vite components while retaining the HTML files as reference docs.

* **Two-database architecture with staging data seeding** The system will use two separate databases, seeding mock data into the staging database to ensure code remains parametric without hardcoding.

### **Details**

* **Review of Attendance Module and Milestones**: JBS Praxis and Tom-Blake Asaah discussed the review of the distributed zip folder, identifying the clock-in and clock-out feature as falling under the attendance milestone ([00:00:00](#00:00:00)). Tom-Blake Asaah clarified that attendance is not limited to workspace time tracking but spans employee self-service, comprehensive monthly attendance views, people registers, and settings such as attendance policies and geofencing ([00:02:09](#00:02:09)).

* **Project Overview and Milestone Structure for My City App ERP**: Tom-Blake Asaah introduced the official start of the My City App enterprise resource planning project, noting that foundational work over the weekend involved Godwin-Okoh Elisha handling the environment and Tom-Blake Asaah managing operational architecture ([00:04:25](#00:04:25)). Tom-Blake Asaah explained that two HTML files were shared via a zip folder at 1:00 or 2:00 a.m., and team members will receive end-to-end ownership of specific modules across 12 structured milestones ranging from milestone 0 to 11 ([00:16:04](#00:16:04)).

  ![][image1]

* **Repository Integration and Attendance Complexity**: Tom-Blake Asaah explained that logic will be pulled from existing repositories like practice local services and Pixel, with core operations drawing over 70 percent of its logic from Pixel, while recruitment and documentation pull from practice local services ([00:20:44](#00:20:44)). Tom-Blake Asaah emphasized the heavy scope of the attendance module, which requires understanding complex underlying engineering across four separate pages including employee self-service, people, settings, and devices ([00:23:17](#00:23:17)).

* **Role-Based Access Control and Mock Data Demo**: JBS Praxis raised a question regarding whether the demo HTML with mock data represents the final visual outcome, which Tom-Blake Asaah confirmed as a mock-data visual of the expected end product ([00:25:39](#00:25:39)). Tom-Blake Asaah and JBS Praxis discussed role permissions, clarifying that while operations and HR managers like Cynthia can view all modules, regular employees are restricted to self-service, home, workspace, staff community, and mailbox features, gated behind a permissions matrix ([00:27:27](#00:27:27)).

  ![][image2]

* **Server Specifications and Technical Architecture Stack**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha presented the server infrastructure, detailing a server configuration of 18 GB RAM and 240 GB SSD space supporting four subdomains: production subdomains \`up.mmyapp.io\` and \`go.mmyapp.io\`, and staging subdomains \`up.staging.mmyapp.io\` and \`go.staging.mmyapp.io\` ([00:31:57](#00:31:57)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha outlined the tech stack consisting of a Node.js backend, BullMQ for workers and schedulers, a PDL hub outbox dispatcher communicating real-time events via sockets, Redis, PostgreSQL 16, Chromium for PDF generation, and NGINX as a reverse proxy ([00:32:59](#00:32:59)).

* **Backend Folder Structure and Autogenerated Contracts**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha detailed the backend structure, including migrations, seeds, shared packages containing autogenerated TypeScript schema contracts to ensure exact naming alignment between frontend and backend, and template folders for generating PDF employment contracts ([00:37:00](#00:37:00)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha added that the system includes IMAP and SMTP email connectivity, an import folder to assist with Excel sheet imports in milestone 2, assets, a staff React app client, a public app, and scripts ([00:38:02](#00:38:02)).

* **System Scripts and Security Considerations for Admin Creation**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha explained that scripts handle one-off system actions such as checks, monitoring, and data provisioning, and can be executed via terminal commands or front-end buttons ([00:41:27](#00:41:27)). Tom-Blake Asaah raised a security concern that creating an admin via script without a full employee payload could create backdoors in the public repository, leading Tom-Blake Asaah to instruct that admin creation scripts must seed a complete employee payload with assigned roles ([00:42:43](#00:42:43)).

* **Deployment, Database Management, and Documentation Guides**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha outlined deployment scripts and database files covering backup, restore, and migration scripts ([00:45:33](#00:45:33)). Tom-Blake Asaah and Godwin-Okoh Elisha discussed the critical absence of a documentation folder, with Tom-Blake Asaah mandating the inclusion of engineering guides, backend and frontend guides, and an auto-updating \`progress.md\` file tracking 85 pages to ensure strict adherence and maintain code quality for AI-assisted development ([00:46:51](#00:46:51)).

* **Source Code Organization, Routing, and Module Gating**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha detailed the source folder structure, including startup server files (\`server.js\`, \`worker.js\`, \`app.js\`), environment and database configurations, the central HTTP route file, and \`module\_loader.js\` ([00:51:43](#00:51:43)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah discussed how module loader and database tags gate access to specific features like announcements, ensuring unassigned users cannot fetch restricted data ([00:52:49](#00:52:49)).

* **Global Pagination Standards and Shared Component Rules**: Tom-Blake Asaah noted that previous projects lacked global pagination, warning that loading excessive unpaginated data could crash the server, and instructed that server-side pagination be locked at a fixed limit of 25 items per page across the entire system ([00:55:00](#00:55:00)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha explained shared components such as money formatting enforcing a strict two-decimal-place limit, noting the structural rule that modules can import from shared components, but shared components cannot import from modules ([00:56:53](#00:56:53)).

* **System Architecture, Services, Real-Time Features, and Background Jobs**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha explains that services operate as independent scripts handling specific tasks such as S3, local, or Google Drive storage configurations, PDF generation, Chromium instances, node mailer dispatchers, encrypted database secrets, and artificial intelligence. Real-time features utilize sockets, rooms, and messaging to enable instantaneous communication without database polling ([00:58:12](#00:58:12)). Additionally, background workers manage jobs, and suggested migration tables are provided for milestone zero, with subsequent milestones 1 through 11 to be added before project commencement ([01:00:48](#01:00:48)).

* **AI Assistant Functional Changes and Data Fetching Limits**: Tom-Blake Asaah notes a significant change from client meetings where the artificial intelligence assistant no longer writes directly to the database; instead, it reads the database and provides deep links to the user interface, such as navigating to a new task creation page ([01:01:43](#01:01:43)). Godwin-Okoh Elisha and Tom-Blake Asaah confirm that a check exists to prevent the artificial intelligence from writing data, restricting its function to data fetching ([01:02:36](#01:02:36)). To prevent timeouts when requesting large datasets like all contacts, Tom-Blake Asaah states that data fetching must be limited in batches (such as 10, 20, or 30\) or respect existing pagination settings like 25 items per batch ([01:03:28](#01:03:28)).

* **Attendance Preparation and Evening Meeting Schedule**: Tom-Blake Asaah reviews the status of end-to-end attendance preparation assigned to JBS Praxis (Love), noting that a full understanding has not yet been achieved. Consequently, Tom-Blake Asaah requests a follow-up meeting at 5:00 p.m. to review the topic further, which Godwin-Okoh Elisha and JBS Praxis ultimately agree to attend ([01:05:15](#01:05:15)).

* **Home Dashboard Module and Role-Sensitive Views**: Tom-Blake Asaah announces that the command center module has been renamed to home to ensure simplicity in module naming. The home dashboard displays attendance over past weeks, weekly needs, partnership pipelines, and key performance indicators connected to organizational and individual goals ([01:07:00](#01:07:00)). Tom-Blake Asaah explains that the dashboard is role-sensitive, tailoring the view based on individual responsibilities, such as Cynthia's operations view or specialized views for the chief executive officer, chief technology officer, and partnership managers ([01:08:07](#01:08:07)) ([01:18:00](#01:18:00)).

  ![][image3]

* **Alert Rules, Monitoring Thresholds, and User Interface Text Management**: Tom-Blake Asaah outlines the alerts module, which allows users to set rules and monitor workflows, such as an attendance rule tracking three late arrivals in 30 days or a partnership inactivity rule set to 30 days. When rules are breached and left uncleared, the dashboard displays metrics like 18 broken attendance rules or 4 days of partnership lateness ([01:09:44](#01:09:44)) ([01:14:33](#01:14:33)). To prevent interface overwhelm, Tom-Blake Asaah instructs that long text blocks must be hidden behind inline icon buttons ([01:09:44](#01:09:44)).

* **Scheduled Reports and Managerial Access**: Tom-Blake Asaah explains that the reports module enables managerial users and the chief executive officer to create scheduled reports, set filters, and automate delivery in PDF or Excel formats to specified mail recipients ([01:12:16](#01:12:16)). Access to these reports is strictly restricted based on user permissions, meaning managers can only view reports relevant to their assigned modules ([01:13:22](#01:13:22)).

* **Dashboard Integration with Staging Database Seeding**: Tom-Blake Asaah explains that while the dashboard falls under milestone one and appears early in development, it requires functional modules like clock-in to be fully wired to display live data ([01:15:31](#01:15:31)). To enable testing before production is ready, mock data will be seeded into the staging database schema across two databases so that components remain parametric rather than hardcoded ([01:16:45](#01:16:45)) ([01:23:43](#01:23:43)).

  ![][image4]

* **Frontend Translation to React and Vite, and Mobile Responsiveness**: Tom-Blake Asaah directs the team to translate the existing HTML reference file into React plus Vite, keeping the HTML file as a reference in the documentation folder. Tom-Blake Asaah notes that current mobile responsiveness is inadequate due to heavy text and sidebar limitations, suggesting that mobile views should incorporate bottom icons and reduced text ([01:19:07](#01:19:07)). Tom-Blake Asaah suggests that Victor could assist with creating a dedicated mobile design ([01:21:27](#01:21:27)).

* **GitHub Repository Setup and Client Data Integration**: Godwin-Okoh Elisha commits to uploading the project to GitHub using the JBS email address and leaving the repository public so participating members can be invited as collaborators ([01:22:27](#01:22:27)). Additionally, Tom-Blake Asaah notes that the client will provide real data, including an organizational staff list detailing full names, job titles, and departments, which will be used to test the import engine ([01:25:46](#01:25:46)).
